condition: Colorectal cancer — rectal bleeding with abdominal pain and weight loss, age 52
permutationLabel: Age 50–59, no change in bowel habit
summary: 52-year-old man with two months of unexplained rectal bleeding mixed with stool, left-sided abdominal pain and 5 kg weight loss; normal bowel habit. NICE NG12: suspected cancer pathway (FIT per DG56).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Blood in the stool and weight loss
inputs.hpi: Two months of dark red blood mixed with the stool most days, cramping left-sided abdominal pain and 5 kg weight loss without trying. Bowels still once a day. No previous colonoscopy. No family history.

exam.abdomen: Soft, mild left iliac fossa tenderness, no mass.
exam.other: PR: dark blood on the glove, no mass.

inputs.socialHistory: Mechanic. Smoker, 10 a day. Drinks 20 units a week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected colorectal cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected colorectal cancer: unexplained rectal bleeding with abdominal pain and weight loss at 52. Suspected cancer pathway.

redFlags.note: NG12 (2015 wording): age ≥ 50 with unexplained rectal bleeding, or ≥ 40 with weight loss and abdominal pain; the triage cancer screen has neither rule.
redFlags.knownGapNote: The triage cancer screen has no "age ≥ 50 with unexplained rectal bleeding" or "age ≥ 40 with weight loss + abdominal pain" rule; its rectal-bleeding rule needs a change in bowel habit (≥ 40, CG27-era wording mislabelled "NICE NG12 1.3.1").
redFlags.proposedFix: Rewrite cancer-screening.ts lower-GI criteria to current NG12/DG56 (FIT-first; ≥ 50 rectal bleeding; ≥ 40 weight loss + abdominal pain; < 50 rectal bleeding + CIBH/weight loss/IDA; rectal/abdominal mass; IDA ≥ 60).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: suspected cancer pathway — age ≥ 50 with unexplained rectal bleeding; age ≥ 40 with unexplained weight loss and abdominal pain (2015 criteria; FIT-first since 2023)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: NICE DG56 — quantitative FIT to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care
guideline.section: FIT to guide referral in symptomatic adults
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Quantitative faecal immunochemical testing to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care (DG56). 2023.

rationale: Permutation: no change in bowel habit, so only the "rectal bleeding ≥ 50" and "weight loss + abdominal pain ≥ 40" criteria apply. Tests that the triage screen covers those NG12 criteria and not only "rectal bleeding + change in bowel habit".
